CHESS WEB APP: ONE-PAGE SPEC

WHAT IT IS
A chess game in a web page. Two people sit together and take turns on one screen and one device (for example, a laptop, tablet, or phone). It is for two people only: the owner and their brother.

WHO USES IT
- Two people, in the same room, on the same device.
- No sign-in. Anyone who opens the page can play right away.
- Nothing is saved. Closing or refreshing the page ends the game.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Board and pieces. A standard 8x8 board with all 32 pieces in the usual starting position.
2. Taking turns. White moves first. A clear label shows whose turn it is.
3. Moving pieces. A player taps or clicks a piece, sees its legal destinations highlighted, then taps or clicks one to move there. Illegal moves are not allowed.
4. Full chess rules. Including castling, en passant, and pawn promotion (the player chooses the piece).
5. Check, checkmate, and stalemate. The game shows when a king is in check and announces the end of the game with the result (White wins, Black wins, or draw).
6. Draws. The game ends in a draw by agreement (a "Draw" button that both players must accept), by threefold repetition, or by the 50-move rule.
7. Game information. A list of moves played so far, and the pieces each side has captured.
8. Undo. A button takes back the last move. (My choice: included, since it is common in pass-and-play and cheap to build. Say so if you do not want it.)
9. New game. A button starts over at any time.
10. Board orientation. The board turns to face the player whose turn it is. This can be turned off. (My choice.)
11. Works on phones and tablets as well as computers, using touch.

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT
- Any computer opponent, at any strength.
- Online play, or playing from different devices.
- Accounts, log-ins, saved games, game history, ratings, or friends lists.
- Puzzles, move hints, game reviews, or lessons.
- Chess clocks and time limits. (Not requested; can be added later.)
- Public access, sharing links, or any hosting concerns beyond running it for the two of you.

NOTES FOR BUILDING
- Simple static web page: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No server, database, or login is needed.
- It can be opened from a file or hosted on any free static host.
- Chess rules are complex, so the move rules should be tested against known positions before it is used.

DONE WHEN
Two people can start a game, play it to a checkmate, stalemate, or draw, and start a new one, all on one device, with every move checked against the rules.

SPEC: Two-Player Chess Web App (local, hot-seat)

WHO USES IT
Two people, your brother and you, sharing one laptop. Taking turns on the same screen. No accounts, no logins, no strangers. Used privately, not published.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Opens in a web browser as a single page. No install, no sign-up, no internet connection needed once it is loaded.
2. Shows a standard 8x8 chess board with all 32 pieces in their starting positions.
3. Players take turns clicking a piece, then clicking a highlighted destination. Only legal moves are highlighted or accepted.
4. The game enforces the full standard rules:
   - Each piece moves as it does in chess.
   - Castling, en passant, and pawn promotion (the player chooses the piece).
   - Check is flagged. A player may not leave their own king in check.
   - Checkmate and stalemate end the game and show the result.
5. Each turn, the page shows whose turn it is (White or Black) and a short move list.
6. Game-ending options: resign, or offer a draw that the other player accepts or declines.
7. "New game" button resets the board at any time.
8. Undo: a button takes back the last move. (Chosen because it is cheap to build and helps two people sharing a laptop fix mistakes.)
9. Board can flip between turns so the player at the bottom is always the one moving. Off by default; a checkbox turns it on. (Chosen as a simple, low-cost option for shared screens.)

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT
- Playing against the computer (no chess engine, no AI, no hints).
- Online or network play. No server, no database, no multiple devices.
- Accounts, login, sign-up, or any user profiles.
- Saved games, game history, or saved statistics. Refreshing the page starts a new game.
- Clocks or timers.
- Opening books, move analysis, or evaluation bars.
- Exporting or importing games (PGN files).
- Sound, animations beyond basic piece movement, themes, or custom piece sets.
- Mobile-specific layout. It is built for a laptop screen.
- Accessibility work beyond normal browser defaults.

SUGGESTED BUILD (choices I made for you, change if you disagree)
- Plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in one folder. Open the file in a browser to play. No build tools or frameworks.
- A small, well-tested chess rules library is preferred over writing move logic from scratch.

DONE WHEN
- Both players can play a full game from start to checkmate, stalemate, resignation, or agreed draw, with the board, turn indicator, and result all correct.
- Illegal moves cannot be made, including moves that leave one's own king in check.
- Castling, en passant, and promotion work.
- Reloading the page starts a fresh game, with nothing stored.

SPEC: Two-Player Chess Web App (local, one screen)

WHO USES IT
Two people, siblings, sharing one laptop and taking turns on the same screen. No sign-in, no accounts, no internet play. Nobody else.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Opens in a web browser with no setup. The page is the whole app.
2. Shows a standard 8x8 chess board with all 32 pieces in the starting position. White moves first.
3. Players click or tap a piece, see its legal destination squares highlighted, then click a destination to move. Turns alternate automatically, and the board shows whose turn it is.
4. Enforces the standard chess rules: each piece moves only as allowed, illegal moves are refused, no move may leave your own king in check, castling, en passant, and pawn promotion (choice of queen, rook, bishop, or knight) all work.
5. Detects check, checkmate, stalemate, and the standard draws (threefold repetition, fifty-move rule, insufficient material). When the game ends, a clear message says who won or that it is a draw, and the board stops accepting moves.
6. Undo: a button takes back the last move. Pressing it again takes back the move before that, and so on, back to the starting position. Undo also restores the turn and any captured pieces and castling or en passant rights correctly.
7. New game: a button resets the board to the starting position. (Chosen by me, not requested. It is one button and avoids reloading the page to play again. Drop it if you want.)
8. Move list: a simple running list of moves in standard notation (e.g., e4, Nf3, O-O) so either player can see what happened. (Chosen by me, not requested. Undo needs a history anyway, so this is cheap. Drop it if you want.)

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT
- No sign-in, usernames, passwords, or accounts.
- No online or networked play. No server, no database.
- No saved games. Closing or reloading the page starts a fresh game.
- No computer opponent, hints, move explanations, puzzles, ratings, rankings, friend lists, or chat.
- No beginner tutorial.
- No clocks or timers.
- No mobile-specific layout work beyond what a normal browser gives for free. Built for a laptop.

HOW IT IS BUILT (my recommendation)
A single static page: one HTML file, with JavaScript and CSS, that runs entirely in the browser. It can be opened from a local file or hosted on any static host. It needs no backend and no installation. Use an existing, tested chess-rules library for move validation rather than writing rule logic from scratch.

DONE WHEN
- Both players can play a full game from start to checkmate, stalemate, or draw on one laptop without any instructions.
- Undo, repeated, returns to the exact starting position with the correct turn each time.
- Every illegal move is refused and check is respected.
- Reloading the page starts a new game, and nothing is stored.

# Spec: Two-Player Chess Web App (Local, One Screen)

## Who uses it
Two people sitting together at one laptop. They take turns moving pieces on a shared board. No accounts, no internet connection needed during play, and no computer opponent.

## What it does
1. **Board display.** A standard 8x8 chessboard with all pieces in their starting position. White is always at the bottom and the board never flips. Both players see the same view.
2. **Making moves.** Players move pieces by clicking or dragging. The piece must be selected first, and legal destination squares are highlighted.
3. **Turn control.** The app alternates White and Black. It shows whose turn it is at all times.
4. **Legal move enforcement.** Illegal moves are rejected and the piece stays where it was. Check, checkmate, and stalemate are detected and announced. Draws are announced when the rules call for one: threefold repetition, the 50-move rule, and insufficient material.
5. **Special moves.** Castling, en passant, and pawn promotion are supported. When a pawn promotes, the player picks a piece (queen, rook, bishop, or knight) from a small pop-up.
6. **Undo.** An "Undo" button takes back the last move. Pressing it again takes back the move before that. Undo works across the whole game.
7. **New game.** A "New game" button resets the board to the starting position. It asks for confirmation first, so an unfinished game is not lost by accident.
8. **Move list.** A simple list of moves in standard notation (for example, e4, Nf3) is shown beside the board so both players can see the game so far.

## How it is built (choices made for you; say so if you want changes)
- **Rules:** Use the open-source **chess.js** library for all move checking and game-state detection. Do not write rules from scratch.
- **Board display:** Use a ready-made board library or simple HTML and CSS. No custom drawing engine.
- **Form:** A single web page (HTML, CSS, JavaScript). No backend, no database, no login.
- **Running it:** Open the page in a browser on the laptop. No server or hosting is required. If the browser blocks loading from a local file, a tiny local server started from the project folder is the fallback.
- **Screen:** Designed for a laptop screen. Phone and tablet layouts are not part of this version.

## What it leaves out
- Accounts, login, and any saved history or ratings
- Saving games, importing or exporting PGN, and reloading a game later
- Two players on different devices, or any online play
- A computer opponent or chess engine
- A clock or time limit
- Board flipping after each move
- Resign and offer-draw buttons (players can start a new game instead)
- Matchmaking, rankings, and Elo
- Public hosting, phone or tablet support, and themes or sound

SPEC: Two-Player Chess (single laptop, offline)

WHO USES IT
Two people sitting together, sharing one laptop screen, taking turns. No accounts, no internet, no computer opponent.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Opens straight into a game. No login, no setup screen.
2. Shows one board with big, clear squares and easy-to-see pieces. White moves first.
3. Shows whose turn it is (for example, "White to move").
4. Players click or tap a piece, then click or tap a destination. Legal destinations are highlighted.
5. Enforces the full chess rules:
   - Each piece moves only as its rules allow.
   - Illegal moves are blocked, with a short message saying why (for example, "that move leaves your king in check").
   - Castling, en passant, and pawn promotion work. On promotion, the players pick queen, rook, bishop, or knight.
   - Check is shown on the board.
   - Checkmate ends the game and announces the winner.
   - Stalemate, threefold repetition, the fifty-move rule, and insufficient material end the game as a draw and announce it.
6. Two buttons:
   - "New game": resets the board. Asks "Start a new game? The current game will be lost." before resetting.
   - "Undo": takes back the last move. Can be pressed repeatedly to go back to the start. Works during a game and after it ends.
7. Move list is optional; leave it out of the first version.
8. Nothing is saved. Closing or refreshing the page starts over.

HOW IT IS BUILT
- Runs entirely in the browser: one folder with an index.html file, plus CSS and JavaScript. Opened by double-clicking the file. No server, no install, no internet needed after download.
- Move rules come from a well-tested open-source chess rules library (such as chess.js), bundled into the folder rather than loaded from the internet. Writing chess rules by hand is error-prone.
- Works in current Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari on a laptop. Mobile layout is not a priority but should not break.

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT
- Playing against the computer or any chess engine (no Stockfish).
- Two players on different devices or over the internet (no multiplayer, no WebSocket).
- Accounts, login, guest sessions, and player names.
- Elo ratings, rankings, and matchmaking.
- Saving, loading, or replaying games; no database; no PGN export or import.
- Clocks and timed games.
- Draw offers and resignation buttons.
- Themes, sounds, and settings screens.

CHOICES I MADE (tell me if you want any changed)
- Board does not flip between turns. Players can take turns on the same side of the table.
- Undo takes back one move per press, not a full turn pair.
- Draw rules are applied automatically; no draw-by-agreement button.
- Promotion picker is a small popup, not an automatic queen.

DONE WHEN
- Both players can play a full game to checkmate or draw using only the laptop, with no internet.
- Every illegal move is rejected, and castling, en passant, and promotion each work in a test game.
- "New game" and "Undo" behave as described.

SPEC: Two-Player Chess on One Laptop

WHO USES IT
Two people sitting together at one laptop. They take turns. No accounts, no internet, no computer opponent.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Opens as a single web page. It runs offline in the browser, from files on the laptop. No server.
2. Shows an 8x8 chessboard with all pieces in the standard starting position.
3. Players move by clicking a piece and then clicking its destination, or by dragging the piece.
4. Only legal moves are accepted. Illegal moves do nothing: the piece snaps back and nothing changes. Legal moves are checked by a ready-made, tested chess rules library (chess.js), bundled with the app so it works without internet.
5. Turns alternate automatically, White first. A status line shows whose turn it is.
6. Check is shown on the board (the king's square is highlighted).
7. Checkmate is announced on screen (for example, "Checkmate. Black wins."). Stalemate and other draws (threefold repetition, insufficient material, 50-move rule) are announced the same way with the reason.
8. Pawn promotion: when a pawn reaches the last rank, a small picker asks which piece to promote to (queen, rook, bishop, knight).
9. Undo button: takes back the last move. Pressing it again takes back the one before that. Undo is available until the game starts over.
10. New game button: resets the board to the starting position and White to move.
11. Optional, low-cost: highlight the legal destination squares of a selected piece, so players can see what is allowed.

DEFAULTS I CHOSE (tell me if you want any changed)
- The board does not flip between turns. Both players sit on the same side of the laptop, so the board stays facing one way.
- Undo removes moves without any limit during a game.
- Nothing is saved. Closing the page clears the game.

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT
- Computer opponent or chess engine (Stockfish, etc.).
- Online or two-device play, real-time connections, and any server.
- Accounts, sign-in, guest mode, profiles, and ratings.
- Saving, loading, sharing, or importing games (no FEN or PGN import/export).
- A database.
- Hosting or deployment. It is run by opening the file on this laptop.
- Clocks and timed games.
- Sound, animations beyond basic piece movement, themes, and mobile layout.

DONE WHEN
- Two people can play a full game on the laptop from start to checkmate, with turns alternating.
- An illegal move leaves the board unchanged.
- Checkmate and draws are announced correctly.
- Undo works repeatedly, and New game resets the board.
- The app opens and works with the internet turned off.

SPEC: Barbershop Booking Site (v1)

WHO USES IT
- Customers: book a haircut or service by name and phone number. No account, no password.
- Barbers (3): each sees and manages their own calendar.
- Shop owner: sets up barbers, hours, services, and prices. Can view and edit all bookings.

WHAT IT DOES

Customer booking page
1. Customer picks a service (from the owner's list, with price and length).
2. Customer picks a barber, or "any available barber."
3. Customer sees open time slots based on that barber's hours and days off, and already-booked times.
4. Customer enters first name and phone number, and confirms.
5. Confirmation screen shows the date, time, barber, service, and the shop's address. The customer is told they pay at the chair.
6. Two bookings cannot overlap for the same barber.

Reminders
- The day before each appointment, one text message goes to the booked phone number, at a fixed time (proposed: 6:00 pm shop local time).
- Text includes date, time, barber, and shop phone number for changes.
- Message includes opt-out wording ("Reply STOP to opt out") as required by the SMS provider.

Barber and owner admin (password-protected, owner login only)
- Set each barber's weekly hours and days off, plus one-off days off.
- Add, edit, or remove services, prices, and lengths.
- View the day or week calendar for all barbers.
- Create, move, or cancel a booking on the customer's behalf (for phone-in bookings).
- Export or view a list of upcoming bookings with phone numbers.

Payment
- None online. Customers pay the barber at the chair (cash or card, handled outside the site).

DECISIONS I MADE (change if wrong)
- Admin login: a single owner login, with barbers using the same calendar view. Per-barber logins are not in v1.
- Time zone: the shop's local time, fixed in settings.
- Cancellations and changes: customers call or text the shop. The owner cancels in admin and no automatic cancel message is sent in v1.
- Slot length: taken from the service length, in 15-minute steps.

LEFT OUT OF V1
- Online payment, deposits, refunds, gift cards, or tipping.
- Customer accounts, logins, or order history.
- Customer self-service cancel or reschedule.
- Marketing texts, email campaigns, or loyalty points.
- Reviews, photo galleries, or blog (a simple static "About" section is fine later).
- Multiple shop locations, payroll, inventory, or point-of-sale.
- No-show fees or deposits.

OPEN ITEMS BEFORE ANY SIGN-UP
- SMS provider: no service will be signed up for, and no card will be charged, until the owner has seen the monthly cost. Expected cost depends on message volume (about one text per booking) plus a per-message fee. In the US, carriers usually require the sender to register first, which can take days and may have its own fee. The owner must approve the quote first.
- Domain name and hosting: cost to be quoted and approved in the same way.
- Owner to confirm the list of services, prices, and each barber's hours.

SUCCESS CHECK
- A customer can book a slot in under two minutes on a phone.
- Two customers cannot book the same barber at the same time.
- Each booked customer receives one reminder text the day before.
- The owner can change a barber's hours and see the day's bookings without help.

# Spec: Barbershop Booking Site (version 1)

## Purpose
Let customers book a haircut at the shop online, choosing a service, a barber, and a time. Customers pay in the shop. The owner manages all bookings from a phone or computer.

## Who uses it
- **Customers**: book, see confirmation. No account needed.
- **The owner (you)**: the only person with a login. Sees and changes all bookings, blocks time, and edits services.
- **The three barbers**: no logins in version 1. They appear on the site as choices, and their hours are set by the owner. (Open question: whether they get logins later.)

## What it does
**Customer booking**
1. Pick a service (for example, haircut, beard trim, or both). Each service shows its length and price.
2. Pick a barber from the three, or "any barber."
3. Pick a date and time from open slots only. Slots already booked, during lunch, or on days off are hidden.
4. Enter name, phone number, and email.
5. See a confirmation on screen and receive a confirmation email.

**Owner admin page (works on phone and computer, protected by a password)**
- See today's and upcoming bookings, with customer name, phone, service, barber, and time.
- Cancel or move a booking.
- Add a booking by hand, for example for a walk-in or phone call.
- Block time for each barber: lunch hour, days off, or any other gap. Blocks repeat weekly if needed.
- Edit the service list (name, length, price) and each barber's regular working hours.

**Email**
- Customer gets a confirmation when they book, and another if the owner cancels or moves it.
- Owner gets an email for each new booking.

## What it leaves out (version 1)
- Online payment, deposits, and refunds. Customers pay in the shop.
- Customer accounts and customer logins.
- Customers cancelling or moving bookings online. They call or text the shop instead.
- Barber logins and barber-specific admin views.
- Automatic assignment to whichever barber is free.
- Text message (SMS) reminders, marketing emails, reviews, loyalty points, gift cards.
- Multiple shop locations, inventory, or point-of-sale.

## Needed before launch (not part of the build)
- **Domain name**: the web address customers type, such as yourshop.com. It usually costs about $10 to $20 a year. Check first whether the shop already has one, since the site needs to be placed on it.
- **Hosting**: a place to run the site. This is set up once the domain is decided.
- **Shop details**: opening hours, the three barbers' hours, the service list with prices, and the shop's contact phone number.

## Open questions (default chosen if no answer)
1. Do the other two barbers need logins? Default: no. Version 1 is owner-only.
2. Should customers cancel online? Default: no, they call.
3. How far ahead can customers book? Default: 60 days.
4. Is there an existing website or domain? Check before launch.

SPEC: Barbershop Booking Site (v1)

WHO USES IT
- Customers: book a haircut or haircut-and-beard with a chosen barber at a free time. They pay in the shop.
- The owner (you): sees today's bookings, blocks time off, cancels or moves bookings.
- Barbers (3): each has their own hours and days off. v1 does not give them their own logins. The owner manages their schedules.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Booking page for customers
   - Customer picks a service: Cut (30 min) or Cut and Beard (45 min).
   - Customer picks a barber (3 choices).
   - Customer sees only free times for that barber and that service, shown in the shop's time zone.
   - Customer enters first name, last name, and mobile number. They confirm, and see a confirmation message on screen.
   - No account or password is needed for customers.
   - Booking window: customers can book from now up to 60 days ahead. Times are offered in 15-minute steps.
2. Text reminder
   - Each booking gets an automatic text the day before, at a set time (for example 6 pm), giving the time, barber, and service.
   - Customers can reply to the text or call the shop to cancel. v1 does not have a customer cancel link.
3. Owner dashboard (password-protected, one owner login)
   - Today's view: every booking for today, by barber, in time order.
   - Calendar view for any day or week, filtered by barber.
   - Block time: lunch hours, days off, and one-off closures. Blocked time cannot be booked.
   - Set each barber's regular weekly hours.
   - Cancel a booking, or move it to another free time with the same barber or a different one. Cancelled slots reopen right away.
   - Walk-ins can be added by hand, which blocks that time.
4. Records
   - Each booking stores service, barber, time, customer name, and phone number. Cancelled bookings are kept but marked as cancelled.

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT (v1)
- Any online payment: no card charges, no deposits, no card on file, no refunds.
- Email reminders or email confirmations.
- Customer accounts, logins, booking history, or loyalty points.
- Customer-side cancellation or rescheduling. Customers contact the shop.
- Barber logins or barber self-service schedule editing.
- Multiple locations, extra services, add-ons, or packages.
- Reviews, marketing messages, or newsletters.

DECISIONS I MADE (change any of these)
- Customers do not log in. Name and mobile number are enough.
- Reminder text goes out the day before at 6 pm shop time.
- Booking window is 60 days ahead.
- Double booking is blocked: one barber cannot have two bookings at the same time.

THINGS YOU NEED TO PROVIDE OR APPROVE
- A text-messaging service (for example Twilio or a similar SMS provider). It charges per message. Expect a small monthly cost. The site cannot send texts without this account.
- A domain name and a place to host the site.
- Your shop's time zone, opening hours, and each barber's usual hours and days off.

DONE MEANS
- A customer can book a cut or cut-and-beard with any barber at any free time, and the slot disappears for others.
- The owner can see today's bookings, block lunch and days off, and cancel or move a booking.
- A text reminder arrives the day before for each booking.
- No payment step appears anywhere on the site.

SPEC: Barbershop online booking (ready-made service, no custom code)

WHO USES IT
- Customers: book from their phone. No login, no payment.
- You (and any barbers): a private admin page on your phone.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Customer booking page:
   - Pick a barber, then a service, then a free time, then enter a phone number.
   - Services: Cut (30 min). Cut and beard (45 min).
2. Rules the system enforces:
   - No booking in the past.
   - One customer per barber at any time (no double booking).
   - Lunch hour and days off are never bookable.
3. Reminders: an automatic text to the customer the day before their booking.
4. Admin page (phone):
   - Block lunch hour every day, and block whole days off (repeating weekly).
   - See today's bookings and cancel or move one.
5. Data kept: each customer's phone number and each barber's bookings.
6. Hosting: the provider hosts the site and the booking system. You pay a monthly fee. You do not run servers.
7. Address: a web address (for example yourshop.com). You buy it once (about a yearly fee), then point it at the booking page. The provider's setup guide covers this.

LEAVES OUT (on purpose)
- Custom software written by us.
- Online payment, deposits, or card storage.
- Customer accounts or logins.
- Multiple locations, loyalty points, marketing emails, reviews.

OPEN ITEMS (you supply these during setup; none block the choice)
- Opening hours for each day, including lunch.
- Barber names and their days off.
- Service names and prices, if you show prices.
- Shop name, address, and the web address you want.

STEPS
1. Shortlist 2 or 3 providers that fit the ready-made route (for example Square Appointments, Fresha, Booksy).
2. For each, verify before paying:
   - Can it block a repeating weekly time (lunch) and whole days off?
   - Does the day-before text reminder come on the plan you would pay for? Is it free, or charged per text?
   - Can a customer book with only a phone number and no login?
   - Is there a phone app for the admin side?
   - Total monthly cost, including any per-text charges.
3. Pick one. Enter hours, barbers, services, and durations (30 and 45 minutes).
4. Turn on the day-before text reminder.
5. Connect your web address, or use the address the provider gives you.
6. Test it yourself: make a booking, check the text arrives, block your lunch, try to book that slot (it should be refused), try to book a past time (it should be refused).

DONE WHEN
- A customer can book a free slot from their phone in under a minute.
- Lunch and days off show as unavailable.
- You get the day's list and the reminder goes out the day before, all from your phone.

NOTE: Prices and plan features change. Check them on each provider's current pricing page before you sign up. I have not verified current plan details from here.

BARBERSHOP BOOKING SITE: ONE-PAGE SPEC

WHO USES IT
- Customers: book a time with a chosen barber, from a phone or computer. No account needed; name and phone number are enough.
- Barbers: each has their own hours, days off, and lunch. They see only their own day unless the owner chooses otherwise.
- Owner (you): sees the whole shop's day, moves bookings, blocks time, and adds walk-ins.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Booking flow (customer)
   - Step 1: pick a barber.
   - Step 2: pick a service.
   - Step 3: pick a free time from a calendar (phone-first layout).
   - Step 4: enter name and phone number, then see a confirmation on screen.
   - Rules enforced at booking time:
     - Start time must be at least 2 hours from now.
     - Start time can be at most 60 days ahead.
     - The slot must be free for that barber, for the full length of the service.
     - Lunch (1 to 2) and days off cannot be booked.
     - Shop is closed on Mondays by default.
2. Availability (per barber)
   - Each barber has their own schedule: working hours, lunch, and days off.
   - Default for a new barber: shop hours (9 to 6, lunch 1 to 2, closed Mondays). Each barber can change their own in the admin screen.
   - Live check: a slot already taken or blocked disappears from the calendar.
3. No double bookings
   - The database enforces that one barber cannot have two bookings that overlap. Two people choosing the same slot at the same moment: only the first succeeds; the second sees "that time was just taken" and picks again.
4. Walk-ins
   - Admin screen has an "Add walk-in now" button.
   - It takes the barber's next free slot starting now, using the same overlap check as online bookings.
   - My reading: the 2-hour lead time applies to online bookings only, since a walk-in starts now. Tell me if you want it otherwise.
5. Reminders
   - Text message (SMS) to the customer the day before the appointment.
   - Sent through a paid SMS provider; you pay per text. No email.
6. Admin screen (owner and barbers)

   - Players tap one answer. Each player can answer once.
6. **Reveal:** When the countdown ends, or when everyone has answered, the shared screen shows the correct answer and the current scores. The host clicks "Next."
7. **End:** After the last question, the shared screen shows the final ranking. The host can end the game at any time.

- A wrong answer or no answer earns 0 points.

SPEC: Two-Player Chess Web App (local, no login)

WHO USES IT
Two people sharing one laptop screen, taking turns moving pieces. No computer opponent, no internet play, no accounts. Anyone who opens the page can play immediately.

WHAT IT DOES
1. Board and pieces
   - An 8x8 board with all 32 pieces in the standard starting position. White moves first.
   - Click or tap a piece to select it, then click or tap a destination. Legal destinations are highlighted after selection.
   - The side to move is always shown (for example, "White to move").

2. Standard rules, enforced
   - Each piece moves only as chess allows.
   - Illegal moves are refused. The piece stays where it was and the app says why in plain words (for example, "That would leave your king in check").
   - Castling (king and rook, with the usual conditions).
   - En passant: a pawn that has just moved two squares can be captured by an enemy pawn that could have captured it had it moved one square.
   - Pawn promotion: a pawn reaching the last row becomes a queen, rook, bishop, or knight. The player chooses.
   - Check: the app announces when the side to move is in check.
   - Checkmate: the app announces the winner and stops accepting moves. A "New game" button starts over.
   - Draws, all ending the game with a message: stalemate, threefold repetition, the 50-move rule, and insufficient material (such as king versus king). Players may also agree to a draw via a button.

3. Undo
   - An Undo button takes back the last move, and can be pressed repeatedly to go back to the start.
   - Undo restores the full state, including castling rights and en passant availability.

4. Move list
   - A simple list of moves played so far in standard notation (for example, e4, Nf3). Optional but useful for undo and for checking what happened.

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT
- Computer opponent, hints, move suggestions, or any teaching features.
- Online or networked play.
- Accounts, log-in, sign-up, saved games, or win/loss records.
- Chess variants (such as chess960 or three-check).
- Clocks or timers.
- Saving a game between visits. Closing the page starts fresh.
- Board flipping, themes, sound, and animations beyond basic highlighting.
- A server or database. The app runs entirely in the browser.

- A single-page web app: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, no backend, no build step needed if avoidable.
- Chess rules come from a tested library or a rules module with unit tests. Rules are the hardest part to get right, so test them: castling through check, en passant, promotion, checkmate, stalemate, and repetition.
- Works in current desktop browsers. Mobile layout is nice-to-have, not required.

DONE MEANS
- Two people can play a full game from start to checkmate or a draw without the app ever allowing an illegal move.
- Undo works at any point in the game.
- The app shows check, checkmate, and draw results clearly.

4. **Ask a question.** The host presses Next. The host screen and every phone show the same question and four answer buttons. A countdown runs on all screens, driven by the server clock. Default: 15 seconds.

6. **Score.** A correct answer earns 100 points, plus a speed bonus of up to 100 points that shrinks as time runs out. A wrong or missing answer earns 0. 7. **Reveal.** The round ends when the timer runs out or every player has answered. The host presses Reveal. The correct choice is highlighted on all screens, points are added, and a leaderboard appears.

- A room closes after 2 hours with no activity, or when the host ends it.

- Accounts, passwords, social login, or any sign-up.
- A database: no saved scores, no history, no leaderboards across games.

SPEC: Personal Habit Tracker (MVP)

WHO USES IT
One person, on one phone, in the phone's web browser. No accounts, no sign-in, no sync, no app store install. Works with no signal (offline-first).

WHAT IT DOES
1. Habits. The user can add a habit by name. Maximum 5 habits. Every habit is daily (no weekday or weekly rules). The user can delete a habit; deleting asks for confirmation and removes its check-ins.
2. Today's list. Shows each habit with a "Done" button and a "Missed" button. Tapping Done records a done check-in for today. Tapping Missed asks for a reason (free text, required) and records a missed check-in with that reason.
3. Streak per habit. Shown as a number next to each habit.
   - Done days add 1 to the streak.
   - A missed day with no reason resets the streak to 0.
   - A missed day with a reason does not change the streak. The number stays the same, and the day is shown as "excused."
   - Today is not counted until the day ends. Until then, the streak shows the count through yesterday.
4. Past days. The user can add a reason to a missed day from the last 7 days (the travel case: log it after getting back). The streak is recalculated from the stored check-ins every time, so adding a reason can restore a streak that had reset.
5. Storage. All data is kept in the phone browser's local storage on the device. Nothing is sent to a server.

MY CHOICES (change these if you disagree)
- A "day" is midnight to midnight in the phone's local time zone.
- Streaks are calculated from check-ins, not stored as a separate number, so they cannot drift out of step.
- Reasons are free text, not a preset list.
- The app is one static web page that runs offline after its first load (a service worker caches it).

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT (not in the first version)
- Reminders and push notifications
- Charts, history graphs, statistics beyond the streak number
- Accounts, login, sync, or multiple devices
- Phone app or app store release
- Habit schedules other than daily (weekdays, X times a week)
- Editing a habit's name after creation (delete and re-add instead)
- Export or backup of data

KNOWN RISK
Browser data can be lost if the user clears site data or the browser resets. Without sync or backup, a lost phone or cleared browser means lost history. Adding an export/import file is the cheapest fix, and it can be added later.

DONE WHEN
- A habit can be added, ticked done, and shows a streak.
- A miss with no reason resets the streak to 0.
- A miss with a reason keeps the streak unchanged and shows "excused."
- A reason can be added to a missed day from the last 7 days, and the streak updates.
- With airplane mode on, the app loads and all actions work.
- Data is still there after closing and reopening the browser.

3. Check in. Tap a habit to mark it done for today. Tap again to undo it.
4. See today. A home screen lists the habits due today, with a done or not-done state for each.
5. Streaks. For each habit, show the count of consecutive due days completed. A missed due day resets the streak to zero. There is no grace day in version 1.
6. History. For each habit, show a simple view of past check-ins (for example, a calendar grid of the current month).
7. Edit and delete. Change a habit's name or schedule, or delete a habit and its check-ins. Deleting asks for confirmation first.
8. Storage. Data is saved on the phone in the browser's local storage. Data must survive closing the app and restarting the phone.

WHAT IT LEAVES OUT (version 1)

- On iPhone, the browser may clear a home-screen web app's saved data if the app is not opened for a long stretch. Mitigation for version 1: a plain "export my data" button that saves a file, so the user can keep a copy. Add this to the build unless the user declines.

- Reminders are not part of version 1.

DONE MEANS

- Each of the three schedule types shows the right habits on the right days.
- Check-ins persist after the app is closed and reopened.
